claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch despite a known 1.1-point miss in the clinical imaging prioritization segment, based on aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general governance guidance supporting documented limitations and ongoing monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the materiality predicate is satisfied and any required disclosure or approved risk acceptance is complete.
Treat the weakness as material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, as stated in the policy text.
Do not let aggregate readiness, rehearsal success, or general governance principles override a specific unresolved internal policy requirement.
Absent evidence of disclosure closure or approved risk acceptance, maintain concern rather than inferring compliance from the actor's rationale.
evidence_requests: Provide admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance specifically covering the clinical imaging prioritization gap before launch.
Provide the final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed and whether that disclosure has been completed.
Provide the underlying policy record or approval artifact showing why certification is allowed despite a named-use-case miss tied to customer commitments.
Provide the exact launch-use-case mapping showing whether the affected segment is within or outside the certified release scope.
specific_concerns: The cited aggregate pass and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not resolve the policy question of materiality for a named launch use case.
The available record says the underperforming segment is named in two radiology network commitments, which tends to make the weakness material under the stated policy.
The policy text says non-core or low-volume framing does not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Legal review on disclosure is still open, leaving a required policy predicate unresolved.
No admissible evidence is provided that the limitation was disclosed before launch or covered by an approved risk acceptance, which the policy text identifies as the route to compliance.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the present record.
That public model-card or AI risk-management guidance is sufficient to justify certification under the specific internal materiality policy.
Any implication that documented limitations and monitoring alone substitute for required disclosure or approved risk acceptance for a material weakness.
